After an election, physical paper ballots may be used to review or confirm the results that
were electronically tabulated and uploaded from the memory cards. The following processes
may occur if necessary:
Hand Counts
Physical ballots are manually counted by hand to confirm the vote totals for selected races.
Risk-Limiting Audits (RLA)
A sample of physical ballots, determined by the SOS, is reviewed and compared to the
reported results to help confirm that the election outcome is accurate.
Recounts
Ballots are counted again for a specific race when a recount is required or requested under
Georgia law by the Superintendent or by a candidate within the required margin
Recanvassing
Ballots may be reviewed or retabulated to help identify and resolve a discrepancy in the
election results.
All of these processes are open to public for observation.
After the election is certified, physical ballots are secured under seal and retained with the
Clerk of Superior Court for two years, as required.

Several election processes are open to public observation, including
Logic & Accuracy testing of voting equipment, ballot transport, and
ballot tabulation activities, recanvassing, hand counts, and recounts.
We welcome Fulton County voters to observe these processes.
Observation hours vary
depending on the
current stage of the
election process.
